stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring, $(A,\mathrm d),(B,\mathrm d)$ dg $R$-algebras, and $N$ a dg $(A,B)$-bimodule. The tensor functor $M\mapsto M\otimes_A N$ from $\operatorname{Mod}_{(A,\mathrm d)}$ to $\operatorname{Mod}_{(B,\mathrm d)}$ defines an exact functor
of triangulated categories
$K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}) \to K(\text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})})$.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; A and B are dg R-algebras; N is a dg (A,B)-bimodule.
conclusions: The tensor functor -⊗_A N induces an exact triangulated functor between the homotopy categories K(Mod_A) and K(Mod_B).

reason: The dg tensor functor is compatible with shifts and mapping cones, as shown by its dg construction; applying the preceding ABC dg-functor exactness principle makes the induced homotopy-category functor triangulated.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be
differential graded $R$-algebras. Let $f : N \to N'$ be a
homomorphism of differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodules.
Then $f$ induces a morphism of functors
$$
1\otimes f :
- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N
\longrightarrow
- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N'
$$
If $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism, then $1 \otimes f$ is an isomorphism of
functors.
hypotheses:
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be
differential graded $R$-algebras. Let $f : N \to N'$ be a
homomorphism of differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodules.
conclusions:
$f$ induces a morphism of functors
$$
1\otimes f :
- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N
\longrightarrow
- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N'
$$
If $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism, then $1 \otimes f$ is an isomorphism of
functors.

reason: For each property-(P) module M, 1⊗f is a natural dg morphism. If f is a quasi-isomorphism, use the exhaustive graded-split filtration of M and short exact sequences of successive stages to reduce to a direct sum of shifts A[k], where tensoring identifies 1⊗f with a shifted f; exact filtered colimits finish.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Property (P) means an exhaustive filtration $0=F_{-1}P\subset F_0P\subset F_1P\subset\cdots$ by dg $A$-submodules with graded-split inclusions and successive quotients isomorphic to direct sums of shifts $A[k]$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be
differential graded $R$-algebras. Let $N$ be a differential graded
$(A, B)$-bimodule which has property (P) as a left differential graded
$A$-module. Then $M \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N$ is computed by
$M \otimes_A N$ for all differential graded $A$-modules $M$.
hypotheses:
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be
differential graded $R$-algebras. Let $N$ be a differential graded
$(A, B)$-bimodule which has property (P) as a left differential graded
$A$-module.
conclusions:
$M \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N$ is computed by
$M \otimes_A N$ for all differential graded $A$-modules $M$.

reason: Uses the signed passage to the opposite algebra to regard the left A-property-(P) module N as a K-flat right A^opp-module. Tensoring any quasi-isomorphism M→M' with N is then a quasi-isomorphism by the derived tensor functoriality lemma, so the ordinary tensor already computes the derived one.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be differential graded $R$-algebras.
Let $N$ be a differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule.
Then the functor
$$
- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N : D(A, \text{d}) \longrightarrow D(B, \text{d})
$$ is a left adjoint to the functor
$$
R\Hom(N, -) : D(B, \text{d}) \longrightarrow D(A, \text{d})
$$.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; A and B are dg R-algebras; N is a dg (A,B)-bimodule.
conclusions: The derived tensor functor -⊗_A^L N:D(A)→D(B) is left adjoint to RHom(N,-):D(B)→D(A).

reason: The previously established dg tensor–Hom adjunction combined with existence/computation of both derived functors yields the derived adjunction under the cited general derived-adjoint-functor lemma. The functor directions and unit/counit are correct.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring and $(A,\mathrm d),(B,\mathrm d)$ differential graded $R$-algebras. Let $N$ be a differential graded $(A,B)$-bimodule.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $N$ defines a compact object of $D(B, \text{d})$, and
\item the map $H^k(A) \to \Hom_{D(B, \text{d})}(N, N[k])$ is an
isomorphism for all $k \in \mathbf{Z}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the functor $-\otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N$ is fully faithful.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; A and B are dg R-algebras; N is a compact dg (A,B)-bimodule in D(B); H^k(A)→Hom_D(B)(N,N[k]) is an isomorphism for every k.
conclusions: The derived tensor functor -⊗_A^L N is fully faithful.

reason: By the tensor–RHom adjunction, full faithfulness reduces to the unit M→RHom(N,M⊗^L_A N). Compactness of N makes its cohomological test preserve sums; a property-(P) filtration reduces to the free shifts A[k], on which the assumed isomorphism H^k(A)→Hom(N,N[k]) establishes the unit.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be differential graded $R$-algebras.
Let $T$ be a differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $T$ defines a compact object of $D(B, \text{d})$, and
\item $S = \Hom_{\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}}(T, B)$
represents $R\Hom(T, B)$ in $D(A, \text{d})$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $S$ has a structure of a differential graded $(B, A)$-bimodule
and there is an isomorphism
$$
N \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} S \longrightarrow R\Hom(T, N)
$$
functorial in $N$ in $D(B, \text{d})$.
hypotheses:
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be differential graded $R$-algebras.
Let $T$ be a differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $T$ defines a compact object of $D(B, \text{d})$, and
\item $S = \Hom_{\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}}(T, B)$
represents $R\Hom(T, B)$ in $D(A, \text{d})$.
\end{enumerate}
conclusions:
$S$ has a structure of a differential graded $(B, A)$-bimodule
and there is an isomorphism
$$
N \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} S \longrightarrow R\Hom(T, N)
$$
functorial in $N$ in $D(B, \text{d})$.

reason: The composition pairing constructs the dg (B,A)-bimodule S=Hom_B(T,B) and natural evaluation c_N:N⊗_B S→Hom_B(T,N). Property-(P) and property-(I) replacements make this a natural derived transformation. Exactness and compactness reduce the isomorphism test to N=B[k], where the assumed computation of RHom(T,B) applies.
